excerpt: May Mobility is an Ann Arbor autonomous ride-hail company running driverless Toyota Siennas with Lyft and others. It agreed in 2026 to go public via a $1.4B SPAC.
content:
May Mobility develops self-driving technology and runs autonomous ride-hail and shuttle services, using modified Toyota Sienna minivans. Rather than launching robotaxis city-wide, it has followed what TechCrunch called a gentle on-ramp: on-demand shuttles and pooled rides on campuses and along simpler routes, then broader ride-hail. In February 2025 it launched its first fully driverless commercial service in Peachtree Corners, Georgia, and it offers rides through Lyft in Atlanta. Its website calls itself an autonomous ride-hail technology company.

May Mobility is based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and was founded in 2017. Cofounder and CEO Edwin Olson previously led Ford's autonomous driving research and co-directed autonomous driving work at the Toyota Research Institute, TechCrunch reported. Toyota led a $50 million investment in 2019. On 16 September 2026 May Mobility announced it would go public by merging with the special purpose acquisition company ACP Holdings Acquisition Corp, in a deal that could raise more than $300 million at a $1.4 billion valuation, TechCrunch and Reuters reported; Reuters said it would list on Nasdaq. TechCrunch said it then operated in three US locations, including Lyft in Atlanta and services in Eden Prairie and Grand Rapids, Minnesota.

Riders pay the fare shown in the Lyft app or the local service's app; May Mobility does not sell directly to consumers and does not publish a price list. Its business customers are cities, transit agencies and ride-hail partners, and it competes with Waymo, Zoox and other robotaxi developers.

We have not used May Mobility for this page. It brings together May Mobility's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
